1	# Handoff: printer and filament calibration in JusPrin
2	
3	Written 2026-10-21 for the agent who implements calibration. Nothing is coded yet; this document records the
4	decisions Kenneth made, the facts verified in OrcaSlicer's code, the design on the canvas, and the smallest build
5	that satisfies both. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` and the documents it lists first; `fork-stewardship.md`
6	governs every line you change outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. This file is untracked on purpose: never commit it.
7	
8	## 1. What a calibration is, in one paragraph
9	
10	A person has a symptom (stringing, under-extrusion, bulging corners) or just wants a filament dialled in. The agent
11	decides whether a test is justified, generates OrcaSlicer's own test geometry into a project of its own, the person
12	prints it and sends a photo, the agent reads the print, and the result is saved as a new preset whose name the person
13	is told to use from now on. The product definition's section 2.11 lists the eight agent steps; this handoff is how
14	they map onto code.
15	
16	## 2. Decisions already made (Kenneth, 2026-10-21)
17	
18	1. A calibration is a project of its own, as long as the person is told what will happen before their project is
19	   closed. Not a plate in the current project (see fact 1 below for why that is impossible without rewriting Orca).
20	2. First batch: temperature tower, flow rate, pressure advance. Nothing else in this iteration.
21	3. The outcome of every test is a new preset: a named copy of the filament (or of the process or printer preset for
22	   the tests that write there). The app does not switch any project to it. The receipt names the preset and the
23	   agent tells the person to pick it from now on.
24	4. No remembered "return to the previous project". The test project is left through Home like any project.
25	5. No per-test UI. Adding a test must be a declaration plus skill text, not page code.
26	6. The physical-print ledger: "doesn't matter, whatever is the easiest". Leave it alone.
27	7. Entry points are hard-coded: a "Calibrate…" row in the project header's printer chip menu, in the filament slot
28	   menu, and in the Home printer card's kebab. A symptom typed in the project chat leads to the same flow.
29	
30	## 3. Facts verified in the code (read, not run)
31	
32	1. **Every OrcaSlicer generator replaces the open project and edits project-wide presets.** `Plater::calib_pa`,
33	   `calib_temp`, `calib_flowrate`, `calib_max_vol_speed`, `calib_retraction`, `calib_VFA`, the input-shaping pair and
34	   `Calib_Cornering` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp` from about line 12677) each call `new_project()` and then write to
35	   `preset_bundle->prints/filaments/printers.get_edited_preset().config`. Plates have no presets of their own, so a
36	   test on a plate of an existing project would change every other plate. Do not try.
37	2. **The test's parameters are runtime-only.** The generator stores them on the current plate's `Print` with
38	   `set_calib_params` (`Print.hpp:1089`); `GCode.cpp` reads them per layer (temperature at line 4697). Nothing writes
39	   them to the 3MF, and loading a project resets the mode to none at `Plater.cpp:5891`. A saved temperature tower,
40	   reopened, slices as a plain tower at one temperature. The pressure-advance pattern is the exception: its per-layer
41	   commands go into the plate's custom G-code, which the 3MF does save. The PA pattern also hard-codes the first
42	   plate's origin (`Plater.cpp:12814`).
43	3. **OrcaSlicer already treats one outcome as a new preset.** The Bambu wizard's save page writes flow results as a
44	   filament preset named "<filament> Flow Rate Calibrated" (`CalibrationWizardSavePage.cpp:37`). Its pressure-advance
45	   results go to the machine, not a preset. The SoftFever dialogs (`calib_dlg.cpp`) save nothing: the person types
46	   the value into a preset by hand.
47	4. **Saving a copy already exists and selects the copy.** `settings_apply_patch` with `persistAs` saves through
48	   Orca's own `Tab::save_preset` and asserts the copy is now selected
49	   (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3356-3369`); the result carries `saved_as`. A stock preset cannot be
50	   overwritten and the preview says so with `read_only_preset` and a suggested copy name (`check_persist`, line
51	   2941). Whether a process-scope copy works end to end is unverified; filament and printer are in use today.
52	5. **Which preset each result belongs to** (from `Preset.cpp`'s option lists): nozzle temperature, flow ratio,
53	   pressure advance, retraction length (as a filament override) and max volumetric speed are filament settings; VFA
54	   writes wall speeds in the process preset; cornering writes junction deviation (process) or jerk limits (printer);
55	   input shaping and Bambu's measured pressure advance live on the machine and produce no preset.
56	6. **The skill mechanism is ready.** `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with a `description:` in its frontmatter is
57	   listed to the model and read on demand through the `skill_read` tool (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1209`,
58	   `AgentHost.cpp:2467`). The four skills that exist today are all trigger-based, so this would be the first
59	   on-demand one. Text limit 16 KiB; one skill per directory; name equals directory name (`skillParser.ts`).
60	7. **The project-replacing path already exists.** The `project_open` tool saves the open project to its version
61	   history, drops unsaved preset edits, and calls `m_plater.new_project(true, true, name)` with confirmations skipped
62	   (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2450-2467`, `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1005`). The generate tool should take the
63	   same route, not a second one.
64	8. **The setup card is already data-driven.** `setup_record` (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1071`) titles the pinned card from a
65	   purpose and headline. A calibration project needs no new pinned card: the agent records the test as the purpose
66	   and the range as the headline.
67	
68	## 4. The design
69	
70	JusPrin v2 canvas, page "Calibration · Printer & Filament": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
71	(nine boards, `calibration-01…08` plus `05b`). The builder that drew them is outside the repo at
72	`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_calibration_page.py`.
73	
74	- Board 1: the three "Calibrate…" rows.
75	- Board 2: a symptom in the project chat. The agent explains, then says in its own words that the current project
76	  will be saved and closed, that the test's settings are temporary, and that nothing is written until the person
77	  chooses. The reply choice is the confirmation.
78	- Board 3: the dialog the menu path shows, carrying the same two facts, because no agent sentence precedes it.
79	- Board 4: the test project. Pinned card from `setup_record`; the agent's first message says what to print and what
80	  to photograph; "Change the range" is the manual control.
81	- Board 5 and 5b: the photo comes back, the agent names the block and why, and proposes one write through the
82	  ordinary settings preview rows plus the preset it is saved as. 5b shows the card is one shape with slots (value,
83	  scope, base preset and printer, setting old → new, the word for what the person picks) and three instances.
84	- Board 6: the receipt with Undo. The agent tells the person the preset name to pick from now on; nothing switches.
85	- Board 7: the test reopened later warns that the steps are not in the file and offers to regenerate.
86	- Board 8: the test on Home as an ordinary project whose status line names the preset it produced.
87	
88	The strings on the boards are illustrations; the agent writes its own. Keep the two facts of board 2 and 3 verbatim
89	in meaning: the project closes, the test's edits are temporary.
90	
91	## 5. The build: one tool, one skill, three rows, one optional seam
92	
93	Do not build: a `calibration_list` tool (the tests are static knowledge; the workspace already reports printer,
94	filament and nozzle), per-test cards, a return hook, preset switching, or Bambu's automatic path. Correct the tool
95	guide (`agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`, the `calibration` table around line 561): the
96	`calibration_generate` row says "onto a new plate", which fact 1 rules out, and `calibration_list` is dropped.
97	
98	### 5.1 The tool: `calibration_generate`
99	
100	One registered tool (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, handler in `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`, adapter work in
101	`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`). Input: `test` (`temperature`, `flow`, `pressure_advance` for now), the
102	test's parameters as Orca's dialogs take them (temperature and pressure advance: `start`, `end`, `step`; pressure
103	advance also `method` line/pattern/tower and `extruderType`; flow: `pass` 1 or 2 and `linear`), and `projectName`.
104	It runs the same release-and-replace sequence as `project_open` (fact 7), then calls the matching `Plater::calib_*`
105	with a `Calib_Params`. Output: the new project's name, the plate and object ids, and the parameters as applied
106	(Orca clamps and substitutes; return what it did). Classify it as a mutation that replaces the project, with the
107	same session-invalidation the open tool has. Mark it in-app only until the MCP side is wanted.
108	
109	The generators call `new_project(false, false, name)` themselves, with confirmations on. Either skip the generator's
110	own call by releasing the project first through the open path and accepting the generator's then-trivial
111	`new_project`, or add a small product-neutral seam so the generator can be told the project is already fresh.
112	Prefer the first; measure before adding a seam. Whatever you do, the version-history save must happen before any
113	preset edit, or the person's project loses its unsaved preset changes.
114	
115	### 5.2 The skill: `AgentUI/src/skills/calibration/SKILL.md`
116	
117	Frontmatter: `name: calibration`, `description:` one line that makes the model read it when a print symptom points
118	at the material or when the person asks to calibrate. Body, in sections:
119	
120	1. When a test is justified, and which symptoms point to which test (stringing and hairs: temperature first,
121	   retraction second; under-extrusion, gaps, bulging corners or top surface: flow; corner bulges and gap at seams at
122	   speed: pressure advance). Say when drying the spool or checking the nozzle comes first.
123	2. Before generating: say the two facts (project saved and closed; temporary settings) and get a reply. From a menu
124	   entry the app has already asked; from a symptom the agent asks.
125	3. Per test: the default range per material, taken from OrcaSlicer's own dialog defaults (`calib_dlg.cpp` has the
126	   PLA, ABS/ASA, PETG, PCTG, TPU, PA-CF, PET-CF sets for temperature); what the person should photograph; how to
127	   read the print; which setting the result writes and in which preset scope; how to name the copy.
128	4. After generating: call `setup_record` with the test as the purpose and the range as the headline, then tell the
129	   person to slice and print and what to photograph.
130	5. Reading the photo: name the best block or tile and why, name the runner-up, and propose one write with
131	   `settings_preview_patch` then `settings_apply_patch` with `persistAs`. Naming rule: "<base> · <printer>
132	   calibrated"; a second test on the same base writes into that copy, never a second name. If the person is already
133	   on their own non-stock preset, writing in place with no new name is an option Kenneth has not ruled on: ask in
134	   the handover, do not decide it in the skill.
135	6. After saving: say the preset's name, that this test uses it now, that other projects keep their filament until
136	   the person picks it, and offer the next test without starting it.
137	7. A reopened test: the steps are not in the file (fact 2); regenerate before slicing again.
138	
139	Keep conversation rules in the skill and one-tool rules in the tool description (`rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs`
140	in memory). Add one line to `skills/print-issues/SKILL.md` pointing at this skill for material symptoms.
141	
142	### 5.3 The entry rows
143	
144	- Project header, printer chip: `Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp` beside "Printer settings…" (about line 176).
145	- Project header, filament slot sub-list: `Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp` beside "Filament settings…" (about line 461).
146	- Home card kebab: `HomeUI/src/components/PrinterMenu.tsx`, the action through `Home/HomeHost.cpp` and
147	  `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` like `open_printer_settings`.
148	
149	A row opens the project chat (the agent pane, not the printer panel: the test needs the project tools) with the
150	confirmation dialog of board 3 first, then a message the person is shown as their own, such as "Calibrate the
151	temperature for Gray PETG on Prusa MK4", so the skill takes over. Use Orca's `MessageDialog`, never
152	`wxMessageBox` (memory: `use-orca-messagedialog`). Every colour and size comes from `ShellTheme` and the tokens.
153	
154	### 5.4 Optional seam: keep the test valid after a reload
155	
156	Fact 2 means a reopened test is a plain tower. Two ways out, pick after measuring: (a) a workspace fact
157	`calibration.generatedThisSession` the skill reads, plus board 7's regenerate offer; or (b) store the `Calib_Params`
158	with the fork's own project data (`Agent/ProjectPersistence`) and re-apply `set_calib_params` on the plate's print
159	after load. (b) removes board 7's warning entirely and is small if the load observer in `Workspace/FileLoads` can
160	run it; the preset edits already come back with the project. The PA pattern's custom G-code needs nothing.
161	
162	## 6. Verification required before calling it done
163	
164	- Adapter test (Catch2, `tests/workspace`): generate each of the three tests from a project with unsaved preset
165	  edits; assert a version was saved first, the new project is named, the plate holds the test objects, and the
166	  print's `calib_params` match the request. Then reload the saved test and assert what fact 2 says, or what seam
167	  (b) fixes.

# Handoff: printer and filament calibration in JusPrin

Written 2026-10-21 for the agent who implements calibration. Nothing is coded yet; this document records the
decisions Kenneth made, the facts verified in OrcaSlicer's code, the design on the canvas, and the smallest build
that satisfies both. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` and the documents it lists first; `fork-stewardship.md`
governs every line you change outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. This file is untracked on purpose: never commit it.

## 1. What a calibration is, in one paragraph

A person has a symptom (stringing, under-extrusion, bulging corners) or just wants a filament dialled in. The agent
decides whether a test is justified, generates OrcaSlicer's own test geometry into a project of its own, the person
prints it and sends a photo, the agent reads the print, and the result is saved as a new preset whose name the person
is told to use from now on. The product definition's section 2.11 lists the eight agent steps; this handoff is how
they map onto code.

## 2. Decisions already made (Kenneth, 2026-10-21)

1. A calibration is a project of its own, as long as the person is told what will happen before their project is
   closed. Not a plate in the current project (see fact 1 below for why that is impossible without rewriting Orca).
2. First batch: temperature tower, flow rate, pressure advance. Nothing else in this iteration.
3. The outcome of every test is a new preset: a named copy of the filament (or of the process or printer preset for
   the tests that write there). The app does not switch any project to it. The receipt names the preset and the
   agent tells the person to pick it from now on.
4. No remembered "return to the previous project". The test project is left through Home like any project.
5. No per-test UI. Adding a test must be a declaration plus skill text, not page code.
6. The physical-print ledger: "doesn't matter, whatever is the easiest". Leave it alone.
7. Entry points are hard-coded: a "Calibrate…" row in the project header's printer chip menu, in the filament slot
   menu, and in the Home printer card's kebab. A symptom typed in the project chat leads to the same flow.

## 3. Facts verified in the code (read, not run)

1. **Every OrcaSlicer generator replaces the open project and edits project-wide presets.** `Plater::calib_pa`,
   `calib_temp`, `calib_flowrate`, `calib_max_vol_speed`, `calib_retraction`, `calib_VFA`, the input-shaping pair and
   `Calib_Cornering` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp` from about line 12677) each call `new_project()` and then write to
   `preset_bundle->prints/filaments/printers.get_edited_preset().config`. Plates have no presets of their own, so a
   test on a plate of an existing project would change every other plate. Do not try.
2. **The test's parameters are runtime-only.** The generator stores them on the current plate's `Print` with
   `set_calib_params` (`Print.hpp:1089`); `GCode.cpp` reads them per layer (temperature at line 4697). Nothing writes
   them to the 3MF, and loading a project resets the mode to none at `Plater.cpp:5891`. A saved temperature tower,
   reopened, slices as a plain tower at one temperature. The pressure-advance pattern is the exception: its per-layer
   commands go into the plate's custom G-code, which the 3MF does save. The PA pattern also hard-codes the first
   plate's origin (`Plater.cpp:12814`).
3. **OrcaSlicer already treats one outcome as a new preset.** The Bambu wizard's save page writes flow results as a
   filament preset named "<filament> Flow Rate Calibrated" (`CalibrationWizardSavePage.cpp:37`). Its pressure-advance
   results go to the machine, not a preset. The SoftFever dialogs (`calib_dlg.cpp`) save nothing: the person types
   the value into a preset by hand.
4. **Saving a copy already exists and selects the copy.** `settings_apply_patch` with `persistAs` saves through
   Orca's own `Tab::save_preset` and asserts the copy is now selected
   (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3356-3369`); the result carries `saved_as`. A stock preset cannot be
   overwritten and the preview says so with `read_only_preset` and a suggested copy name (`check_persist`, line
   2941). Whether a process-scope copy works end to end is unverified; filament and printer are in use today.
5. **Which preset each result belongs to** (from `Preset.cpp`'s option lists): nozzle temperature, flow ratio,
   pressure advance, retraction length (as a filament override) and max volumetric speed are filament settings; VFA
   writes wall speeds in the process preset; cornering writes junction deviation (process) or jerk limits (printer);
   input shaping and Bambu's measured pressure advance live on the machine and produce no preset.
6. **The skill mechanism is ready.** `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with a `description:` in its frontmatter is
   listed to the model and read on demand through the `skill_read` tool (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1209`,
   `AgentHost.cpp:2467`). The four skills that exist today are all trigger-based, so this would be the first
   on-demand one. Text limit 16 KiB; one skill per directory; name equals directory name (`skillParser.ts`).
7. **The project-replacing path already exists.** The `project_open` tool saves the open project to its version
   history, drops unsaved preset edits, and calls `m_plater.new_project(true, true, name)` with confirmations skipped
   (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2450-2467`, `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1005`). The generate tool should take the
   same route, not a second one.
8. **The setup card is already data-driven.** `setup_record` (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1071`) titles the pinned card from a
   purpose and headline. A calibration project needs no new pinned card: the agent records the test as the purpose
   and the range as the headline.

## 4. The design

JusPrin v2 canvas, page "Calibration · Printer & Filament": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
(nine boards, `calibration-01…08` plus `05b`). The builder that drew them is outside the repo at
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_calibration_page.py`.

- Board 1: the three "Calibrate…" rows.
- Board 2: a symptom in the project chat. The agent explains, then says in its own words that the current project
  will be saved and closed, that the test's settings are temporary, and that nothing is written until the person
  chooses. The reply choice is the confirmation.
- Board 3: the dialog the menu path shows, carrying the same two facts, because no agent sentence precedes it.
- Board 4: the test project. Pinned card from `setup_record`; the agent's first message says what to print and what
  to photograph; "Change the range" is the manual control.
- Board 5 and 5b: the photo comes back, the agent names the block and why, and proposes one write through the
  ordinary settings preview rows plus the preset it is saved as. 5b shows the card is one shape with slots (value,
  scope, base preset and printer, setting old → new, the word for what the person picks) and three instances.
- Board 6: the receipt with Undo. The agent tells the person the preset name to pick from now on; nothing switches.
- Board 7: the test reopened later warns that the steps are not in the file and offers to regenerate.
- Board 8: the test on Home as an ordinary project whose status line names the preset it produced.

The strings on the boards are illustrations; the agent writes its own. Keep the two facts of board 2 and 3 verbatim
in meaning: the project closes, the test's edits are temporary.

## 5. The build: one tool, one skill, three rows, one optional seam

Do not build: a `calibration_list` tool (the tests are static knowledge; the workspace already reports printer,
filament and nozzle), per-test cards, a return hook, preset switching, or Bambu's automatic path. Correct the tool
guide (`agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`, the `calibration` table around line 561): the
`calibration_generate` row says "onto a new plate", which fact 1 rules out, and `calibration_list` is dropped.

### 5.1 The tool: `calibration_generate`

One registered tool (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, handler in `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`, adapter work in
`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`). Input: `test` (`temperature`, `flow`, `pressure_advance` for now), the
test's parameters as Orca's dialogs take them (temperature and pressure advance: `start`, `end`, `step`; pressure
advance also `method` line/pattern/tower and `extruderType`; flow: `pass` 1 or 2 and `linear`), and `projectName`.
It runs the same release-and-replace sequence as `project_open` (fact 7), then calls the matching `Plater::calib_*`
with a `Calib_Params`. Output: the new project's name, the plate and object ids, and the parameters as applied
(Orca clamps and substitutes; return what it did). Classify it as a mutation that replaces the project, with the
same session-invalidation the open tool has. Mark it in-app only until the MCP side is wanted.

The generators call `new_project(false, false, name)` themselves, with confirmations on. Either skip the generator's
own call by releasing the project first through the open path and accepting the generator's then-trivial
`new_project`, or add a small product-neutral seam so the generator can be told the project is already fresh.
Prefer the first; measure before adding a seam. Whatever you do, the version-history save must happen before any
preset edit, or the person's project loses its unsaved preset changes.

### 5.2 The skill: `AgentUI/src/skills/calibration/SKILL.md`

Frontmatter: `name: calibration`, `description:` one line that makes the model read it when a print symptom points
at the material or when the person asks to calibrate. Body, in sections:

1. When a test is justified, and which symptoms point to which test (stringing and hairs: temperature first,
   retraction second; under-extrusion, gaps, bulging corners or top surface: flow; corner bulges and gap at seams at
   speed: pressure advance). Say when drying the spool or checking the nozzle comes first.
2. Before generating: say the two facts (project saved and closed; temporary settings) and get a reply. From a menu
   entry the app has already asked; from a symptom the agent asks.
3. Per test: the default range per material, taken from OrcaSlicer's own dialog defaults (`calib_dlg.cpp` has the
   PLA, ABS/ASA, PETG, PCTG, TPU, PA-CF, PET-CF sets for temperature); what the person should photograph; how to
   read the print; which setting the result writes and in which preset scope; how to name the copy.
4. After generating: call `setup_record` with the test as the purpose and the range as the headline, then tell the
   person to slice and print and what to photograph.
5. Reading the photo: name the best block or tile and why, name the runner-up, and propose one write with
   `settings_preview_patch` then `settings_apply_patch` with `persistAs`. Naming rule: "<base> · <printer>
   calibrated"; a second test on the same base writes into that copy, never a second name. If the person is already
   on their own non-stock preset, writing in place with no new name is an option Kenneth has not ruled on: ask in
   the handover, do not decide it in the skill.
6. After saving: say the preset's name, that this test uses it now, that other projects keep their filament until
   the person picks it, and offer the next test without starting it.
7. A reopened test: the steps are not in the file (fact 2); regenerate before slicing again.

Keep conversation rules in the skill and one-tool rules in the tool description (`rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs`
in memory). Add one line to `skills/print-issues/SKILL.md` pointing at this skill for material symptoms.

### 5.3 The entry rows

- Project header, printer chip: `Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp` beside "Printer settings…" (about line 176).
- Project header, filament slot sub-list: `Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp` beside "Filament settings…" (about line 461).
- Home card kebab: `HomeUI/src/components/PrinterMenu.tsx`, the action through `Home/HomeHost.cpp` and
  `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` like `open_printer_settings`.

A row opens the project chat (the agent pane, not the printer panel: the test needs the project tools) with the
confirmation dialog of board 3 first, then a message the person is shown as their own, such as "Calibrate the
temperature for Gray PETG on Prusa MK4", so the skill takes over. Use Orca's `MessageDialog`, never
`wxMessageBox` (memory: `use-orca-messagedialog`). Every colour and size comes from `ShellTheme` and the tokens.

### 5.4 Optional seam: keep the test valid after a reload

Fact 2 means a reopened test is a plain tower. Two ways out, pick after measuring: (a) a workspace fact
`calibration.generatedThisSession` the skill reads, plus board 7's regenerate offer; or (b) store the `Calib_Params`
with the fork's own project data (`Agent/ProjectPersistence`) and re-apply `set_calib_params` on the plate's print
after load. (b) removes board 7's warning entirely and is small if the load observer in `Workspace/FileLoads` can
run it; the preset edits already come back with the project. The PA pattern's custom G-code needs nothing.

## 6. Verification required before calling it done

- Adapter test (Catch2, `tests/workspace`): generate each of the three tests from a project with unsaved preset
  edits; assert a version was saved first, the new project is named, the plate holds the test objects, and the
  print's `calib_params` match the request. Then reload the saved test and assert what fact 2 says, or what seam
  (b) fixes.
- Settings test: a preview with `persistAs` on a stock filament reports `read_only_preset` with the copy name;
  apply with the copy name saves and selects it; a second apply with the same copy name updates it (no second copy).
- Page tests (Vitest): the skill parses, is listed with its description, and stays under the size limit.
- Prompt tests, like `tests/printer_prompt` and `tests/project_prompt`: a symptom message leads to the two facts
  and a reply choice before any generate call; a photo turn leads to exactly one preview and one apply with the
  naming rule. Record requests with the shell harness; no live-model batch without Kenneth approving it (memory:
  `prompt-eval-spend-budget`).
- One shell-harness run with `--manual-mcp` driving `calibration_generate` and the settings tools end to end on the
  fake Bambu printer (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`).
- The three rows open the chat and show the dialog; the dialog's Cancel leaves the project untouched.

## 7. Open questions for Kenneth

1. Write in place when the person is already on their own preset, or always a named copy?
2. Should the generate tool be offered over MCP in this iteration, or in-app only?
3. Seam (a) or (b) in 5.4, once you have measured (b).

## 8. Pointers

- Product definition 2.11, 3.3 and 4.2: `agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`.
- Tool and skill rules: `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`, sections "Decide whether this should be a
  tool" and "Skills versus tools".
- Memory notes: `calibration-design-decisions`, `use-orca-messagedialog`, `rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs`,
  `prompt-eval-spend-budget`, `temp-docs-stay-untracked-and-visible`.

36	   test on a plate of an existing project would change every other plate. Do not try.
37	2. **The test's parameters are runtime-only.** The generator stores them on the current plate's `Print` with
38	   `set_calib_params` (`Print.hpp:1089`); `GCode.cpp` reads them per layer (temperature at line 4697). Nothing writes

---
name: windows-build-machine
description: "Facts about the Windows Server 2022 machine used for JusPrin Windows verification (no admin, RDP at 100%, no GPU, toolchain and Mesa locations)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1e908987-3ebc-4e47-9372-ca2af82d4fee
  modified: 2026-09-16T05:20:39.573Z
---

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.
- The permission guard refuses `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` (it reports it as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. Hand build-tree deletion to the user; build trees there contain `resources` symlinks into live worktrees, so unlink those before any recursive delete.
- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].

Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.

npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.

The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.

To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
(skips the npm requirement above) plus
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six
bridge/registry sources and `main.cpp`. `vswhere.exe` is **not** installed; vcvars is at
`C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`
and cmake at `C:\tools\cmake\bin\cmake.exe`. Point the Python suite at the result with
`JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<dir>\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe`; the whole suite runs in ~8 s.

An **existing** build tree configured before node was installed keeps `JUSPRIN_NPM:FILEPATH=JUSPRIN_NPM-NOTFOUND`
in its CMakeCache, and `find_program` never retries a cached NOTFOUND -- so the next build fails at
configure with the `npm not found` FATAL_ERROR even once npm is on PATH. Reconfigure the tree once with
`cmake . -DJUSPRIN_NPM="C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/npm.cmd"`; putting node on PATH alone
is not enough. Neither the Bash tool nor a PowerShell session started before 2026-09-16 inherits the user
PATH entry, so prefix `$env:PATH` explicitly in each invocation.

**Shared build tree (2026-09-17):** other Claude sessions build and commit from `C:\src\JusPrin` and
`C:\src\JusPrin\build` concurrently. Do not patch that checkout or build there from a worktree session;

name: crash-stacks-without-a-debugger
description: "Get a symbolized call stack for a native crash on the Windows box in minutes: C:\\b\\minidbg (Win32 debug API) plus a build tree compiled with /Z7 and linked /DEBUG; traps that cost a full rebuild"
metadata:

  originSessionId: c04fbdd1-d707-42dc-922c-7911bb1d35e0
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:09:52.100Z
---

`C:\b\minidbg\minidbg.exe <exe> [args]` (source `minidbg.cpp` beside it, built with `cl /std:c++17 /EHsc /DUNICODE`) runs a program under the Win32 debug API and prints a symbolized stack, with file:line where a PDB exists, for every access violation, heap corruption, stack-buffer overrun and second-chance exception. No WinDbg download needed. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1`. `run-harness-example.ps1` there shows the env setup for the shell harness. Used 2026-10-14 to find the Check Print crash: the stack led straight to `GCodeViewer::init` → `strlen(glGetString(GL_VERSION))` with no current GL context.

For line numbers you need a tree with debug info. Configure with
`"-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE=/MD /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG /Z7"`, the same for C, and `"-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_RELEASE=/DEBUG:FULL /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF"` (example: `C:\b\ckp-build.cmd`). **Keep `/MD`.** Overriding the flags without it compiles everything `/MT`, and the link fails only at the very end with `LNK2038 RuntimeLibrary mismatch` against opencv/libcurl, after a 40-minute build. `SLIC3R_MSVC_PDB` is declared in CMakeLists.txt but nothing reads it.

Quick triage without any of this: the event-log fault offset in a system DLL maps to a function via `dumpbin /exports <dll>` (the nearest export at or below the offset). ucrtbase `0x2a341` is `strlen+0x31`, meaning a null or bad `char*`.

Run harnesses with `Start-Process -RedirectStandardError` rather than PowerShell `2>`. A PowerShell native-command redirect writes the file only when the process exits, so a hung run shows a 0-byte log. Visible windows of a stuck process can be listed with `C:\b\ckp-windows.ps1 -ProcessId <pid>` (a `#32770` titled 引导_P21 is OrcaSlicer's setup guide left open).

Windows GL fact found the same day: `wxGLCanvas::Create` on MSW always ends with `wglMakeCurrent(nullptr, nullptr)`. Creating any GL canvas leaves no context current, so GL work right after constructing a canvas needs an explicit make-current first. Upstream's helper for this is `GLCanvas3D::_set_shown_canvas_current`.

See [[windows-build-machine]].

name: entire-commit-hook-hangs
description: "git commit hangs in Entire's prepare-commit-msg on Windows because Entire opens CONIN$ for a [Y/n] link prompt; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 makes it non-interactive"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 673eb384-7139-489f-8ef7-aa76f6ab7efa
  modified: 2026-09-27T05:53:11.186Z
---

Root cause (diagnosed 2026-09-25, Entire CLI 0.11.0): when the committing session has file changes to link,
`entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` shows "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n]" and reads the
answer from `CONIN$`, not stdin. The agent's Git Bash has a hidden console, so the open succeeds and the read blocks forever.
`</dev/null` does not help. Commits with nothing to link skip the prompt, which is why it looked intermittent.
The log is buffered, so `.entire/logs/entire.log` shows nothing until the process exits.
Evidence: handle dump of the hung process showed a `\Device\ConDrv` handle with a blocked synchronous read.
Entire's own Pi integration prefixes agent bash commands with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for this exact reason.
With `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` the same hook finished in ~0.3s and added the trailer, 3 of 3 runs; without it, 3 of 3 hung.

**Why:** It looks like a slow checkpoint condense, so it is easy to wait a long time for nothing.
A separate, real slowdown also exists: an `msbuild -m` build pins all 16 cores (processor queue ~64) and every
`entire` launch then takes 5-20s. That is slow, not hung; don't confuse the two.

**How to apply:** Fixed 2026-09-25: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is set as a user env var (HKCU\Environment), so Claude and Codex
shells inherit it after the app restarts (verified in Claude: 3/3 hook runs 0.3s with trailer). If a commit hangs again, first check
`echo $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` in the agent shell. Restarting the Claude app: the tray has no Quit, so end all `claude` processes
from a helper launched via WMI (outside Claude's tree) and relaunch with `explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`.
If one hangs anyway, kill only that commit's `entire` PID; never `--no-verify`. See [[windows-build-machine]].

2026-09-27: with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` already set, a `git merge --no-ff` (merge commit) in a worktree still ran past a
120 s `timeout` -- but the merge commit was already written correctly and nothing was left running. After a timeout, check
`git log -1` and the parents before retrying; a retry would make a second commit. A plain `git commit` minutes earlier took ~seconds.

guard, then the user immediately found two things I never tried: the Agent chat panel
was still on screen, and clicking a project card led nowhere useful. Both were one
click away.

validated.

  `PrintWindow` lies about GL and modals; `CopyFromScreen` of the window rect does not.

  the real bridge, and it found two more defects the guards could not.
- Run the screen's primary gesture end to end in the app before calling UI work done,

  editor, `no_warn_when_modified_gcodes=true` suppresses the customized-preset modal,

description: "Facts about the Windows Server 2022 machine used for JusPrin Windows verification (no admin, RDP at 100%, no GPU, toolchain and Mesa locations)"
metadata:

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.
- The permission guard refuses `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` (it reports it as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. Hand build-tree deletion to the user; build trees there contain `resources` symlinks into live worktrees, so unlink those before any recursive delete.
- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].

Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.

npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.

The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.

To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
(skips the npm requirement above) plus
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six
bridge/registry sources and `main.cpp`. `vswhere.exe` is **not** installed; vcvars is at
`C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`
and cmake at `C:\tools\cmake\bin\cmake.exe`. Point the Python suite at the result with
`JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<dir>\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe`; the whole suite runs in ~8 s.

An **existing** build tree configured before node was installed keeps `JUSPRIN_NPM:FILEPATH=JUSPRIN_NPM-NOTFOUND`
in its CMakeCache, and `find_program` never retries a cached NOTFOUND -- so the next build fails at
configure with the `npm not found` FATAL_ERROR even once npm is on PATH. Reconfigure the tree once with
`cmake . -DJUSPRIN_NPM="C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/npm.cmd"`; putting node on PATH alone

name: crash-stacks-without-a-debugger
description: "Get a symbolized call stack for a native crash on the Windows box in minutes: C:\\b\\minidbg (Win32 debug API) plus a build tree compiled with /Z7 and linked /DEBUG; traps that cost a full rebuild"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: c04fbdd1-d707-42dc-922c-7911bb1d35e0
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:09:52.100Z
---

`C:\b\minidbg\minidbg.exe <exe> [args]` (source `minidbg.cpp` beside it, built with `cl /std:c++17 /EHsc /DUNICODE`) runs a program under the Win32 debug API and prints a symbolized stack, with file:line where a PDB exists, for every access violation, heap corruption, stack-buffer overrun and second-chance exception. No WinDbg download needed. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1`. `run-harness-example.ps1` there shows the env setup for the shell harness. Used 2026-10-14 to find the Check Print crash: the stack led straight to `GCodeViewer::init` → `strlen(glGetString(GL_VERSION))` with no current GL context.

For line numbers you need a tree with debug info. Configure with
`"-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE=/MD /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG /Z7"`, the same for C, and `"-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_RELEASE=/DEBUG:FULL /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF"` (example: `C:\b\ckp-build.cmd`). **Keep `/MD`.** Overriding the flags without it compiles everything `/MT`, and the link fails only at the very end with `LNK2038 RuntimeLibrary mismatch` against opencv/libcurl, after a 40-minute build. `SLIC3R_MSVC_PDB` is declared in CMakeLists.txt but nothing reads it.

Quick triage without any of this: the event-log fault offset in a system DLL maps to a function via `dumpbin /exports <dll>` (the nearest export at or below the offset). ucrtbase `0x2a341` is `strlen+0x31`, meaning a null or bad `char*`.

Run harnesses with `Start-Process -RedirectStandardError` rather than PowerShell `2>`. A PowerShell native-command redirect writes the file only when the process exits, so a hung run shows a 0-byte log. Visible windows of a stuck process can be listed with `C:\b\ckp-windows.ps1 -ProcessId <pid>` (a `#32770` titled 引导_P21 is OrcaSlicer's setup guide left open).

Windows GL fact found the same day: `wxGLCanvas::Create` on MSW always ends with `wglMakeCurrent(nullptr, nullptr)`. Creating any GL canvas leaves no context current, so GL work right after constructing a canvas needs an explicit make-current first. Upstream's helper for this is `GLCanvas3D::_set_shown_canvas_current`.

See [[windows-build-machine]].

name: entire-commit-hook-hangs
description: "git commit hangs in Entire's prepare-commit-msg on Windows because Entire opens CONIN$ for a [Y/n] link prompt; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 makes it non-interactive"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 673eb384-7139-489f-8ef7-aa76f6ab7efa
  modified: 2026-09-27T05:53:11.186Z
---

Root cause (diagnosed 2026-09-25, Entire CLI 0.11.0): when the committing session has file changes to link,
`entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` shows "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n]" and reads the
answer from `CONIN$`, not stdin. The agent's Git Bash has a hidden console, so the open succeeds and the read blocks forever.
`</dev/null` does not help. Commits with nothing to link skip the prompt, which is why it looked intermittent.
The log is buffered, so `.entire/logs/entire.log` shows nothing until the process exits.
Evidence: handle dump of the hung process showed a `\Device\ConDrv` handle with a blocked synchronous read.
Entire's own Pi integration prefixes agent bash commands with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for this exact reason.
With `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` the same hook finished in ~0.3s and added the trailer, 3 of 3 runs; without it, 3 of 3 hung.

**Why:** It looks like a slow checkpoint condense, so it is easy to wait a long time for nothing.
A separate, real slowdown also exists: an `msbuild -m` build pins all 16 cores (processor queue ~64) and every
`entire` launch then takes 5-20s. That is slow, not hung; don't confuse the two.

**How to apply:** Fixed 2026-09-25: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is set as a user env var (HKCU\Environment), so Claude and Codex
shells inherit it after the app restarts (verified in Claude: 3/3 hook runs 0.3s with trailer). If a commit hangs again, first check
`echo $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` in the agent shell. Restarting the Claude app: the tray has no Quit, so end all `claude` processes
from a helper launched via WMI (outside Claude's tree) and relaunch with `explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`.
If one hangs anyway, kill only that commit's `entire` PID; never `--no-verify`. See [[windows-build-machine]].

2026-09-27: with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` already set, a `git merge --no-ff` (merge commit) in a worktree still ran past a
120 s `timeout` -- but the merge commit was already written correctly and nothing was left running. After a timeout, check
`git log -1` and the parents before retrying; a retry would make a second commit. A plain `git commit` minutes earlier took ~seconds.

name: verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app
description: "On JusPrin UI work, exercise the screen's primary click path in the running app and validate the capture method first; unit tests and static screenshots hid basic defects."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: eca70b1c-f154-4c03-a3df-ca667a82efcc
  modified: 2026-09-12T16:42:17.903Z
---

On the Home screen (2026-09-12) I shipped a review-ready branch after passing every
guard, then the user immediately found two things I never tried: the Agent chat panel
was still on screen, and clicking a project card led nowhere useful. Both were one
click away.

**Why:** I checked the *page* against the mockup instead of the *screen*, and I stopped
at "synthetic input is blocked on this machine" instead of finding another way in.
Worse, my capture method was `PrintWindow`, which renders OpenGL content black **and
omits modal dialogs entirely** — so my "verification" screenshots were structurally
blind to exactly the defects that were there. I verified with an instrument I never
validated.

**How to apply:**
- Before trusting a screenshot, prove the capture shows what is really on screen.
  `PrintWindow` lies about GL and modals; `CopyFromScreen` of the window rect does not.
- Drive the page's own controls over the WebView2 DevTools protocol when the OS refuses
  synthetic input: launch with `REDACTED`,
  then `Runtime.evaluate` a real `element.click()` on the target. See
  [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]]. That click goes through the real handler and
  the real bridge, and it found two more defects the guards could not.
- Run the screen's primary gesture end to end in the app before calling UI work done,
  and compare the whole window against the design, not just the surface you wrote.
- Config levers that remove blockers without clicking: `default_page=1` lands on the
  editor, `no_warn_when_modified_gcodes=true` suppresses the customized-preset modal,
  `backup_switch=false` stops the restore prompt.

  modified: 2026-09-28T18:48:29.778Z
---

When fixing one visible failure (e.g. a system-prompt bug in one conversation mode), Kenneth expects the fix to be judged against every related scenario, not just the reported one. He said (2026-09-28) that I tend to solve the problem in front of me and break "a lot more situations" that aren't in view, and asked me to research best practice online instead of reasoning from the one bug.

**Why:** On the printer-panel prompt this was borne out: a two-line fix for the Change conversation silently took Add-mode `add-not-now-done` from 19/20 to 3/20; only a side-by-side full-suite run caught it.

**How to apply:**
- Before editing a shared prompt/component, build or extend a test set covering all its scenarios (off-script inputs, regressions from git history), then compare old vs new in the same run (`tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --prompt-rev HEAD`).
- Scope a fix to the scenario it's for; keep measured wording for the others byte-identical.
- Don't let the current bug drive general recommendations — look for external best practice first.

name: write-reports-in-plain-english
description: "Kenneth finds dense, jargon-heavy status reports very hard to read; restate in plain English with common-sense reasoning, not tables of counts"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 71e3bd46-c856-4b36-b7cc-979fe94e0bdf
  modified: 2026-10-14T00:50:18.008Z
---

On 2026-10-14, after a long run of experiment reports on the project assistant's prompt, Kenneth said: "You have to restate everything in plain English, it's very difficult to read your text."

The reports he was reacting to were packed with tool names, arm names, "3 of 3" counts, tables and compressed bullet labels.

**Why:** he reads these to decide what to do next, often quickly, and he judges results by whether the explanation makes sense in the real world ("the rubber has to meet the road"), not by the numbers from a small test set. He said the same day that with small samples "we cannot just look at the numbers... we need to use common sense to see if the attribution makes sense."

**How to apply:** (my interpretation) write to him in ordinary sentences. Say what happened and why it makes sense, as you would to someone who was not watching. Keep code identifiers, arm names and counts to the few that carry the point, and explain a term the first time it appears. Lead with the answer. Prefer a short explanation of cause over a table of outcomes. When passing work to sub-agents, tell them the same: judge by whether the cause is believable, and check results against how the product is really used. See [[fix-without-breaking-other-scenarios]].

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.
# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.

### 5. One seam beats many touch points

**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.

### 10. Pull direction dominates every local edit

**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.

**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.

**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them
into the strip at construction. The Phase 1 production shell reached a
19-added-line upstream footprint this way where the POC's reparenting shell
needed edits across eight upstream files.

The same measurement gives the rule for every fork-owned screen that comes
after the shell. OrcaSlicer's surfaces (the stock homepage, Prepare, Preview,
Monitor, the settings tabs) stay inside the Notebook, because their
correctness depends on it. Fork-owned surfaces (the header, the Agent pane,
Home, and whatever follows) live outside it, as siblings of the Notebook in a
fork-owned sizer, shown and hidden by the shell. The shell *reads* the
Notebook's selection to decide what to show and *never edits its page list*:
no `RemovePage`, `InsertPage`, or reparenting of a stock page. Removing or
replacing a page hands the fork the meaning of that index. Upstream keeps
addressing it by number — `tpHome` as a dialog parent, the target of
`EVT_LOAD_URL`, the tab `post_init` returns to — and every one of those lands
on the fork's widget with no conflict and no error. If a fork surface truly
must be a page, append it last, where no upstream code addresses it.

Navigation between screens stays a Notebook selection change even when the
screen being left is fork-owned. Menu and shortcut enabling, undo and redo
availability, and slice-status updates all read `GetSelection()`, so the
selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.
Showing Prepare any other way leaves those predicates answering for the wrong
page, silently.

Some stock behavior is already exposed as an event idiom rather than a
function. Upstream itself drives plate slicing from two places with the same
sequence — the slice button and the Cmd+R shortcut both run
`plater->update(true, true)`, post `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_SLICE_PLATE` to the Plater,
and select the Preview tab — so fork code may repeat that short dispatch
without violating the shared-implementation rule; the behavior itself stays
owned by Plater's event handler.
